source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
I traced the USB nets in the KiCad and I think I found the cause. The
USBLC6-2SC6 ESD chip (U3) has pin 5 (VBUS) connected to GND instead of
+5V. The D+/D- routing itself looks correct: connector A6/B6/A7/B7,
through U3, to ESP GPIO20 (D+) / GPIO19 (D-).

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
My concern is that with the VBUS pin grounded, the chip's internal
steering diodes would clamp D+ and D- to about 0.7V, so the lines can
never reach the 3.3V USB levels and the host never sees the device.
That matches the symptom exactly.

Could this be the problem? If so, the fix would be to route U3 pin 5
to VBUS (+5V) instead of GND. I am going to lift that pin on one sample
to confirm.

Thanks

execution.observed_behavior: The grounded VBUS pin on U3 clamps the protected USB data lines to approximately 0.7V, preventing valid USB signaling and device detection.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
For the proper fix so we keep the ESD protection: correct the symbol
so pin 5 (VBUS) goes to +5V and pin 2 to GND separately (not tied
together), keeping the D+/D- pass-through through U3. With a correctly
wired USBLC6 the protection is back and USB works. Does that match
what you'll change? No rush, I'll keep testing in the meantime.

value_updates.u3_supply_pin_isolation: pin 2 and pin 5 are separate nets

execution.observed_behavior: Freelancer reports that the agreed U3 ESD-protection wiring correction has been completed.

routing_warnings.description: This verifies native USB operation only after U3 was removed and the data lines were bridged; it does not verify retained ESD protection.
This verifies enumeration and flashing with U3 removed, so the result supports native USB operation rather than USB data-line ESD protection.
